findings.title: Success-path test only loosely checks the forwarded upstream envelope
findings.detail: The happy-path assertion only checks `{ success: true }`, so a route that fabricated its own success envelope instead of returning apiServer's result verbatim (as the spec requires) would still pass; tighten to `toEqual` against the stubbed upstream reply (`code: 'CREATED'`, `data.id: 1` + forwarded fields).

findings.title: No test pins that only allowlisted fields are forwarded upstream
findings.detail: `toMatchObject(validPayload)` passes even if extra keys are sent upstream, so a future switch to a passthrough schema or spreading the raw `body` would go uncaught despite the spec requiring exactly `{name,email,message,created_at}`; add a case posting extra keys (e.g. `id`, `isAdmin`) and assert `Object.keys(sent).sort()` equals `['created_at','email','message','name']`.

findings.title: Malformed-JSON test does not assert the distinguishing error code
findings.detail: It asserts only `success: false`, so the dedicated `INVALID_JSON` branch at src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts:39 is not distinguished from a validation failure; add `code: 'INVALID_JSON'` to the `toMatchObject`.

findings.title: Upstream error text returned verbatim to anonymous callers
findings.detail: On `res.success === false` the route returns the upstream's `code` and `message` unchanged (src/libs/api/server.ts:22-23 copies `error.message` through); existing proxy routes behave the same, but this is the first route reachable by anonymous visitors, so internal upstream error text (e.g. a database message) would be shown publicly. Fix-forward: return a fixed message such as `{ success:false, code:'SUBMIT_FAILED', message:'Pesan gagal dikirim, coba lagi', data:null }` and log the upstream code server-side only.
